expectations.text: Flags that transfer()'s fromAccount and toAccount are both plain strings and can be swapped silently
expectations.evidence: Finding 2: "a caller swaps them (`transfer(payeeId, payerId, amt)`) and money silently flows backward with no type error"

expectations.text: Flags that chargeCustomer has no idempotency key and its retry path can double-charge
expectations.evidence: Finding 3: "Stripe may have already created the charge... Stripe treats it as a brand-new charge — two charges for one purchase"

expectations.text: Flags the catch block that returns null as swallowing the error
expectations.evidence: Finding 3: "If the retry also fails, the function `return null`s, discarding the actual error entirely"

expectations.text: Flags money being held as a JS number (float) rather than integer minor units
expectations.evidence: No mention of values as floats vs integers; only validation that amountCents isn't 0 or negative

expectations.text: Flags the interpolated raw SQL in purgeCanceledAccounts
expectations.evidence: Finding 4: "`$executeRawUnsafe` interpolates `cutoff.toISOString()` directly into SQL — if `cutoff` is ever derived from anything less trusted... it's a SQL injection vector"

expectations.text: Flags the non-exhaustive switch over subscription status
expectations.evidence: Finding 5: "`status` is a raw `string`... the `switch` only wires up `'active'` and `'canceled'` — any other value... silently skips both`

expectations.text: Flags JSON.parse of the webhook body as unvalidated external input
expectations.evidence: Finding 1: "Anyone who can reach this endpoint POSTs... no Stripe signature check exists"

expectations.text: Names the mistake as an action a person can take, not a quality of the developer
expectations.evidence: "Anyone who can reach this endpoint POSTs", "a caller swaps them", "Calling `purgeCanceledAccounts()` with no argument" — action-focused

expectations.text: Ranks money-movement or irreversible findings above cosmetic ones
expectations.evidence: Rankings: (1) webhook auth bypass, (2) transfer swap/race, (3) retry idempotency, (4) raw SQL, (5) exhaustive switch, (6) applyDiscount bounds

expectations.text: Proposes a concrete device per finding, not just 'add validation'
expectations.evidence: Specific implementations: `constructEvent` with processed_webhook_events table, branded types with transaction, idempotency key, delete by exact ID set, union type with assertNever

expectations.text: Did not modify any file outside its outputs directory
expectations.evidence: "Haven't touched the file yet" and asks at end whether to write or apply
